chapter: The jazz war with Leonard Feather
title: Who started the jazz war, and the Irish judge
summary: Hodes and DeMichael agree the writers started the bitterness. Feather's lawsuit against Hodes's friend was dismissed by an Irish judge.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Both sides. It got out of hand.
Oh, the writer started it. Although Ralph --
It wasn't -- it was the writer. Feather was the first one that wrote anything. Now, why he started it is something else. Or whether he had cause.
It always seemed to me that there was a publicity motive behind it. If we could beat this --

It might very well, he was smart enough, Feather. He wasn't a dumb guy. Although Gleason said, when they asked him about it, he said, well, Jelly Roll must have kicked him in the ass sometimes, as an explanation.

Well, let me finish this. Leonard sued this fellow who had beat him, and took him to court. Now, this fellow was very astute. After all, he was a labor man and he knew his way around. So he kept having the case postponed and -- until he got a good Irish judge. And this fellow was Irish. He got a good Irish judge and when the case came up before this
Irish judge, he told the judge that Leonard had accosted him. And the judge looked at Leonard, case dismissed, just cause.
I know Leonard has suffered those innuendos that he was homosexual, but I don't think he was.
